skill.name: spawn
skill.description: Launch AI coding agents or generic CLI commands in new terminal sessions across macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.
skill.summary: Open external agent and command sessions with optional output capture.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The launcher intentionally executes commands, but several platform paths interpolate commands and working directories into shells without validation. Most documentation, UUID, /proc, path, and obfuscation alerts are false positives. Cookbooks also default to bypassed approvals, while conversation summaries can reach external agents without a redaction step.

remediation.issue: Shell command strings accept unvalidated command and working-directory values.
remediation.suggestion: Use argument arrays where possible, quote every shell boundary, validate working directories, and require confirmation before executing user-derived commands.

remediation.issue: Provider cookbooks disable approval and sandbox protections by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default to sandboxed, approval-enabled modes. Require explicit user consent for force mode or approval bypass flags.

remediation.issue: Temporary scripts and captured output use shared paths without lifecycle controls.
remediation.suggestion: Use private temporary directories, exclusive creation, mode 0600, and guaranteed cleanup after completion.

remediation.issue: Conversation history can be forwarded to external providers without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit consent, remove secrets and private context, and preview the summary before sending it to another provider.

semantic_findings.title: Approval and Sandbox Bypass Enabled by Default
semantic_findings.description: The Codex cookbook says to always bypass approvals and sandboxing, while the Cursor cookbook enables force mode. Spawned agents can modify files and execute commands without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cookbooks explicitly prescribe flags that disable or bypass interactive safety controls. Their command examples apply these flags to agentic tools with filesystem and shell capabilities.

semantic_findings.title: Conversation History Forwarded Without Redaction
semantic_findings.description: The workflow copies conversation history into a prompt and sends it to another AI agent. It provides no secret filtering, scope review, or privacy warning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly instructs the caller to copy conversation history and pass it as the external agent prompt. No redaction or preview step appears in the cited instructions.

content.user_title: Launch Agents and Commands in New Terminals
content.value_statement: Interactive tools and long-running commands can block the current coding session. This skill opens them in separate terminals and optionally captures their output.
actual_capabilities: Spawns supported AI CLIs in new terminal windows using provider-specific cookbooks.
Runs generic CLI commands in separate terminal sessions.
Supports macOS Terminal, Windows Terminal, WSL, tmux, and a background-process fallback.
Captures clean agent output or full debug output in temporary files.
Detects selected provider authentication failures and opens login commands.
Reads completed output with a configurable timeout.
limitations: Executes constructed shell commands and does not validate or restrict their contents.
Requires installed terminal applications, tmux, and requested CLI tools.
Windows capture behavior is limited, and platform fallbacks differ.
Temporary output and script files are not automatically removed or permission-hardened.

use_cases.title: Delegate a coding task
use_cases.description: Launch a selected coding agent in another terminal while keeping the primary session available.

use_cases.title: Start a long-running command
use_cases.description: Run builds, media processing, or diagnostics in a separate interactive terminal.

use_cases.title: Test provider workflows
use_cases.description: Open provider CLIs, complete authentication, and capture responses for evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Run one command
prompt_templates.prompt: Open a new terminal in {working_directory} and run {command}. First verify the command syntax with its help option.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate to one agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn {provider} in a new terminal for this task: {task}. Follow its cookbook and keep approval prompts enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Capture an agent response
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn {provider} for {task}, capture clean output, wait up to {timeout} seconds, then summarize the result and report the output location.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two agent reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch Claude Code and Codex separately to review {scope}. Use sandboxed modes, capture both responses, and compare agreements, differences, and unresolved risks.

output_examples.input: Run the project test suite in a separate terminal.
output_examples.output: A new terminal opens in the project directory and starts the requested test command.

output_examples.input: Ask Codex to review the authentication flow and capture its response.
output_examples.output: Codex starts in a separate session. Its response is captured to a temporary file for later review.

output_examples.input: Open the Cursor login flow after an authentication failure.
output_examples.output: A new terminal opens with the supported Cursor login command and waits for authentication.

best_practices: Confirm the exact command, working directory, and provider before launching.
Use sandboxed modes and approval prompts unless the user explicitly authorizes broader access.
Remove temporary output files promptly and avoid storing secrets in captured logs.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted text directly into shell commands.
Do not disable sandbox and approval controls by default.
Do not forward conversation history until sensitive values are removed and the user confirms.

faq.question: Which operating systems are supported?
faq.answer: The launcher includes paths for macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux environments with tmux or background-process fallbacks.

faq.question: Which AI agents can it launch?
faq.answer: The included cookbooks cover Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot.

faq.question: Can it run non-AI commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The terminal child skill launches generic CLI commands such as builds, scripts, diagnostics, and media tools.

faq.question: Where is captured output stored?
faq.answer: Output is stored in platform temporary directories and returned by path or read after completion.

faq.question: Does it validate commands before execution?
faq.answer: No. It recommends checking help output, but the launcher executes the constructed command string without content validation.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: It can open supported provider login commands, but each provider CLI manages credential storage and authentication.
